summary:
R U OK? (Are You OK?) is a local-first health self-assessment tool for astronauts and others living in isolated or extreme settings. We built it as a prototype for the challenge "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions."

The app adapts to its environment: ISS, Moon, Mars, Earth, hospital or nursing home. Thresholds, protocols and vocabulary ("astronaut", "patient", "resident") live in configuration files, not code. Members complete quick physical and psychological check-ins and get a traffic-light status. Unknown, stale or lost data is never shown as green, so the global status is the worst of health and connectivity. Guided meditation and breathing exercises with voice support wellbeing, and an SOS works without login.

It runs 100% offline on FastAPI and React, with no cloud or CDN dependency. Writes are idempotent and queued, so no data is lost. A simulated Earth link models communication delay, and behavioral details stay private unless the member shares them or there is an emergency. A control center and mobile devices connect over the local network.

It matters because crews on the Moon or Mars cannot count on real-time ground support. Autonomous, trustworthy monitoring helps detect problems early, and the same design serves hospitals and elder care. R U OK? is not a medical device, and every clinical threshold is cited in the project's sources.
details:
What it does and how it works

R U OK? is a self-assessment app. A member (astronaut, patient or resident, depending on the environment) completes short check-ins on physical and psychological health. A pure-function assessment engine compares the answers with thresholds defined per environment (ISS, Moon, Mars, Earth, hospital, nursing home) and returns a traffic-light status per body system. The global status is the worst of health and liveness: unknown, stale or lost data is never green.

Three kinds of user work over the local network:

- Member (mobile-first): check-ins, trends, guided interventions (breathing, meditation with voice guidance), kudos and badges.

- Medic: reviews members and alerts.

- Control center: a multi-device view fed in real time by Server-Sent Events.

An SOS works without login. A simulated Earth link (comm_link) queues anything addressed to external levels and applies the communication delay, as it would on a real Moon or Mars mission.

Benefits and intended impact

Crews far from Earth cannot rely on real-time ground support. The app gives them early, autonomous, understandable detection of physical and mental problems. The same architecture serves hospitals and elder care, because the environment is configuration, not code. Our goal is for the crew to be the first line of care.

Tools and technologies

- Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLModel, SQLite (WAL), pytest, uv, ruff.

- Frontend: React 18, Vite 6, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, React Router, Zustand, Recharts, Framer Motion, IndexedDB (idb), openapi-fetch, Vitest.

- Other: OpenAPI contract as the source of truth with generated types, Docker Compose, Makefile, GitHub Actions CI (3 checks), GitHub Kanban. No special hardware: phones and laptops on a LAN.

Creativity

- One generic members model that changes vocabulary and clinical rules per environment.

- Offline-first design with an IndexedDB outbox and client-generated UUIDs, so writes are idempotent and nothing is lost.

- A time-accelerated demo clock and a simulated communication delay.

- Behavioral privacy: mood details are hidden outside the member unless shared or in an emergency.

- Wellbeing interventions with voice guidance.

Factors we considered

- Local-first: no cloud, CDN or internet at runtime. Fonts, icons and images are bundled.

- Real devices: phones connect over plain HTTP without a secure context, so we avoid service workers and HTTPS-only APIs.

- Security: the backend always validates role and data ownership, and the front end only adapts the UX.

- Safety: this is not a medical device. The disclaimer is always visible and each clinical threshold is cited in docs/sources.md.

- Teamwork: small PRs, mandatory CI and a feature freeze before the presentation.
